newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil February trade gap could hit $2 bln - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil February trade gap could hit $2 bln - paper.

text.p: Brazil's foreign trade deficit swelled to $1.2 billion in the first 16 days of February and could reach a negative $2 billion by the end of the month, O Globo daily reported.

O Globo columnist Miriam Leitao said an unnamed member of the government economic team explained the higher than expected trade gap saying January purchases by state oil monopoly Petrobras had only being registered this month.
Without considering the Petrobras purchases, Brazil's trade deficit so far this month would be of around $700 million, the newspaper quoted the official as saying.
O Globo said the latest figures confirmed forecasts of a very high trade deficit for all of 1996.

The newspaper said that traditionally Brazil's trade accounts remained relatively balanced during the first quarter and that the country usually produced a trade surplus in the second quarter when a large number of commodity exports moved through ports.
Brazil posted a $413 million trade deficit in January, the Industry and Commerce Ministry reported earlier this month.
